targets.title: Alignment snap guides

definition.markdown:
### A1 — Alignment snap guides

- **What it does:** while dragging, candidate alignments to other cards'
  centres/edges (and equal-gap rhythms) render as temporary guide lines and
  the drag settles onto them inside a threshold. Grid snap remains a
  separate toggle.
- **Reference behavior:** tldraw SnapManager (`SnapManager.ts:35`,
  BoundsSnaps/HandleSnaps, `SnapIndicatorOverlayUtil.ts:22`); Excalidraw
  threshold model `SNAP_DISTANCE = 8` screen px scaled `8/zoom`
  (`packages/excalidraw/snapping.ts:41-50`). The thin geometry already
  exists unused in the cradle (`interactions.ts:207-239` returns
  `{position, guides}`).
- **Landing seam:** wire `snapPosition` (m0m5/canvas) into the live drag
  path (`researchInstruments.tsx:527,530` groupMove calls) and the vendored
  canvas's overlay; guides drawn viewport-side, never persisted.
- **UI harmonisation:** guide lines in the canvas's existing hairline
  colour pair; no text, no badge.
- **Acceptance:** fixture canvas with 3 cards; drag a 4th — a guide renders
  while within threshold, position settles, no guide remains after release;
  screenshot pair (mid-drag / released) as evidence; grid toggle unaffected.

targets.title: Shape, sticky and text vocabulary

definition.markdown:
### A2 — Shape, sticky and text vocabulary

- **What it does:** the canvas holds more than note/image cards: sticky
  notes (colour set, editable label), basic shapes (rectangle, ellipse,
  diamond, at minimum) and standalone text objects — all presentation
  material on the same occurrence grid, movable, alignable, frameable.
- **Reference behavior:** tldraw geo enum
  (`TLGeoShape.ts:40-62`) and sticky (`TLNoteShape.ts:30-35`); Excalidraw's
  element set (`types.ts:215-231`); Miro's sticky palette (doc-cited).
- **Landing seam:** extend the `ResearchCard` union inside
  `oi.research-scene/v1` (`researchMaterial.ts:26-29`; closed-key
  validation at `:81` gains the new card kinds); tool row gains a compact
  shape/sticky picker in the existing icon grammar.
- **UI harmonisation:** shapes default to the quietest style (no fill or
  one fill); sticky colours come from the app's token palette, not
  web-whiteboard primaries. No new chrome beyond one picker.
- **Acceptance:** create one of each kind, move/align/frame them, commit;
  reload — kinds and styles survive the material round-trip; validation
  rejects unknown kinds with the existing closed-key error.

targets.title: Connector kinds, routing and labels

definition.markdown:
### A3 — Connector kinds, routing and labels

- **What it does:** connections between cards can be straight, curved or
  elbow (orthogonal, rerouting around moved endpoints) and can carry an
  owner-written label at the midpoint.
- **Reference behavior:** tldraw arrow `kind: 'arc' | 'elbow'`
  (`TLArrowShape.ts:21`, elbow router `arrow/elbow/getElbowArrowInfo.tsx`)
  and arrow labels; Excalidraw elbow arrows (`elbowArrow.ts`); Miro
  connector shapes/labels (doc-cited).
- **Landing seam:** the connection create menu (`researchInstruments.tsx:499-507`)
  gains kind + label acts; kind/label/waypoints persist as
  presentation material keyed by the existing edge ids; semantic relation
  kind and directionality keep flowing through the native ops unchanged.
- **UI harmonisation:** kind shown as three small line glyphs; label styled
  like card caption text (small, quiet); no permanent label chrome.
- **Acceptance:** draw one connector of each kind between two cards; drag
  an endpoint card — elbow reroutes with no manual waypoints; label renders
  at midpoint and clears when emptied; the native relation receipt for the
  same edge is byte-identical before/after (presentation overlay only).

### A5 — Minimap on the canvas

- **What it does:** a corner minimap shows all content plus the live
  viewport rectangle; click/drag on it jumps the camera.
- **Reference behavior:** tldraw shipped minimap
  (`DefaultMinimap.tsx:23`, `MinimapManager`, click-to-jump at `:164`).

  (`researchInstruments.tsx:477-483` semantic zoom source); shared
  implementation with C2 (graph minimap).

  honours reduced-motion.

  content; clicking jumps the camera to the point; viewport rect tracks
  camera travel; no layout shift of the tool row.

- **What it does:** one act fits all content (or the selection) with
  margin; persistent ± controls and keyboard zoom/reset; zoom percentage
  readable on demand.

  kin); Miro zoom-to-fit (doc-cited).

  ceiling 4× to be revisited); add fit-selection/fit-all acts + controls.

  percentage appears transiently on zoom, then fades (no standing text).
- **Acceptance:** fit-all with 50 scattered cards leaves every card fully
  visible with margin at any window size; keys +/−/0 work; percentage
  flashes and fades; canvas camera easing preserved.

- **What it does:** a search act over card text, frame titles and shapes;

  SearchOverlay pattern (`src/knowledge/SearchOverlay.tsx`) as the

  and selects it; a second match cycles with Enter; no match leaves a
  quiet empty state; selection written through the existing host.select
  seam so identity holds.

targets.title: Presentation over frames

definition.markdown:
### A8 — Presentation over frames

- **What it does:** saved frames become an ordered, presentable sequence:
  present from a frame, arrow advances the camera to the next frame's
  bounds (fullscreen), Esc exits; order is the saved frame order.
- **Reference behavior:** Miro Present frame-to-frame (doc-cited); tldraw
  frame camera + frame headings (`FrameShapeUtil.tsx:305`); the audit's
  reader law (real fullscreen via `requestFullscreen`, focus over chrome).
- **Landing seam:** frames already save ordered (`saveFrame`,
  `researchInstruments.tsx:383`; `frameOrder` in named views `:385-386`);
  add a present act + fullscreen host frame; sequencing stays
  session-local (as the existing walk already does, `:508-520`) unless the
  owner promotes it into the material record.
- **UI harmonisation:** presenting hides every panel (the audit's focus
  law); frame transition is a camera ease, never a cut effect; no
  auto-advance, no timer.
- **Acceptance:** three frames → present starts fullscreen at frame 1;
  arrow travels to frame 2's bounds; Esc restores the editor exactly;
  reduced-motion shortens the ease.

### A8 — Presentation over frames

- **What it does:** saved frames become an ordered, presentable sequence:
  present from a frame, arrow advances the camera to the next frame's
  bounds (fullscreen), Esc exits; order is the saved frame order.
- **Reference behavior:** Miro Present frame-to-frame (doc-cited); tldraw
  frame camera + frame headings (`FrameShapeUtil.tsx:305`); the audit's
  reader law (real fullscreen via `requestFullscreen`, focus over chrome).
- **Landing seam:** frames already save ordered (`saveFrame`,
  `researchInstruments.tsx:383`; `frameOrder` in named views `:385-386`);
  add a present act + fullscreen host frame; sequencing stays
  session-local (as the existing walk already does, `:508-520`) unless the
  owner promotes it into the material record.
- **UI harmonisation:** presenting hides every panel (the audit's focus
  law); frame transition is a camera ease, never a cut effect; no
  auto-advance, no timer.
- **Acceptance:** three frames → present starts fullscreen at frame 1;
  arrow travels to frame 2's bounds; Esc restores the editor exactly;
  reduced-motion shortens the ease.

targets.title: Frame headings on stage

definition.markdown:
### A9 — Frame headings on stage

- **What it does:** a frame may carry a written title rendered quietly at
  its top edge, editable in place — the only default text this programme
  adds to the stage, and only when the composer names the frame.
- **Reference behavior:** tldraw frame name rendering
  (`FrameShapeUtil.tsx:305`); Obsidian group label (`label` field).
- **Landing seam:** `ResearchFrame` gains an optional title (material
  record, closed-key validation extended); rendered by the vendored frame
  layer.
- **UI harmonisation:** small caption style; empty title renders nothing
  (no placeholder on stage).
- **Acceptance:** title a frame — it renders at the frame edge, survives
  commit/reload; clearing it removes all trace; frames with no title look
  exactly as today.

targets.title: Embed and media cards

definition.markdown:
### A10 — Embed and media cards

- **What it does:** cards can hold a bounded web embed (URL-ref, sandboxed
  iframe) or a media reference — the canvas becomes a place where sources
  can be seen, not only cited.
- **Reference behavior:** Excalidraw `embeddable`/`iframe` element types
  (`types.ts:115-140`); Miro embeds (doc-cited).
- **Landing seam:** new `ResearchCard` kinds in the material record; embeds
  store the URL (never a fetched copy — the kernel's material protocol
  serves bytes only for possessed files); strict sandbox attributes;
  pruning law applies unchanged (`researchMaterial.ts:76-78`).
- **UI harmonisation:** embed chrome is a hairline frame + the existing
  card colour system; no vendor badges.
- **Acceptance:** paste a URL → embed card renders interactively; removing
  the source occurrence prunes the card from every frame and saved view
  (existing law); a disallowed scheme is refused at validation with the
  existing error style.

targets.title: Save schedule for the research scene

definition.markdown:
### B1 — Save schedule for the research scene

- **What it does:** commits happen on a schedule, not only per-action: a
  short trailing autosave after a gesture settles, immediate on a
  destructive act or lens switch, flush on quit. The acknowledgement gate
  and queued-edit guard are unchanged.
- **Reference behavior:** Excalidraw's local-first debounced saves; the
  decided Obsidian T2 posture (2 s trailing autosave, immediate on
  command/leaf-switch, flush-on-quit — recreation-backlog D-1/T2), tuned to
  the cradle's native-owner commit.
- **Landing seam:** around `commitResearch()` (`app.ts:1070`) and the
  gesture batching (`researchInstruments.tsx:269-285`); the queued-edit
  guard (`:299`) and read-through refusal (`nativeWorkspace.ts:255`)
  govern every scheduled commit identically.
- **UI harmonisation:** a single quiet save-state glyph (saved / saving /
  held) in the existing status line; no modal, no toast on routine saves.
- **Acceptance:** script ten quick gestures — one commit lands after the
  settle window (receipt count as evidence); quit mid-burst flushes or
  honestly reports the held state; a changed-native-composition refusal
  surfaces once, draft retained (existing message, `app.ts:1070`).

targets.title: Canvas document interchange: Obsidian `.canvas`

definition.markdown:
### B2 — Canvas document interchange: Obsidian `.canvas`

- **What it does:** export the composed scene to a `.canvas` file and
  import an Obsidian-authored `.canvas` into the canvas lens — the
  constellation travels to the tool the owner already uses, by reference
  never by lock-in.
- **Reference behavior:** the documented Obsidian format, pinned from the
  possessed app: nodes `{id, type: "text"|"file"|"link"|"group", x, y,
  width, height, …}`; edges `{id, fromNode, toNode, fromSide, toSide, …}`
  (bundle offsets 2431562, 1171612; RE-TARGETS §3).
- **Landing seam:** an export/import act beside save view (`:433-437`),
  mapping cards→text nodes, images→file/text nodes, frames→group nodes,
  connections→edges with sides; A2/A3 presentation kinds degrade honestly
  (dropped fields documented in the export header), semantic relations
  never export as plain edges without their native identity note.
- **UI harmonisation:** two icon-grammar acts; no format settings panel.
- **Acceptance:** export a fixture scene → open the file in possessed
  Obsidian 1.7.7: every card/frame/connection appears with position and
  grouping; round-trip a small hand-authored `.canvas` into the lens:
  nodes/edges/positions preserved; invalid JSON refused at validation with
  a named error.

targets.title: Honest drift on saved views

definition.markdown:
### B4 — Honest drift on saved views

- **What it does:** applying a named view whose members have changed
  reports the drift quietly (which members left since saving) instead of
  silently dropping them; the view keeps its identity basis.
- **Reference behavior:** the dead model's `viewDrift` (`view.ts:142-149`)
  — the designed behavior the live canvas replaced with silent pruning
  (`researchMaterial.ts:76-78`); Obsidian's occurrence-count honesty in
  the link cache (A3).
- **Landing seam:** `applyView` (`researchInstruments.tsx:386`) gains a
  post-prune notice; named views keep the refs that pruned (tombstones)
  in the material record.
- **UI harmonisation:** one status-line sentence, never a modal; the view
  still applies.
- **Acceptance:** save a view over 3 members; delete one; re-apply —
  camera and remaining selection restore, status names the departed
  member; the notice is dismissible and repeats no other time.

- **What it does:** from a card or selection bound to a native subject,
  one act opens the M0′ graph centred on that subject with its
  neighbourhood emphasised — completing the one-field round trip that
  today only runs graph→canvas (`techneHandoff.ts:15-56`).
- **Reference behavior:** Obsidian's local graph around a note (A3 F6);
  the lane's own law: "No export, no second canvas … returns by
  reference" (`techneHandoff.ts:1-6`).
- **Landing seam:** the inverse ask through the one wiki projection
  selection ask; KnowledgeSurface opens with `techneHandoff`-style basis
  (subject_ref + origin "canvas").
- **UI harmonisation:** an icon-grammar context act; no dialog.
- **Acceptance:** from a constellation card, the act opens the graph
  centred on the same subject_ref (evidence: the reading's node id equals
  the card's subject basis); back-navigation returns to the canvas with
  camera and selection intact; no re-import, no duplicate node.

targets.title: Relation vocabulary made visible on emphasis

definition.markdown:
### C4 — Relation vocabulary made visible on emphasis

- **What it does:** edges carry their relation kind as a quiet label shown
  on hover/emphasis (and in C3's neighbourhood view) — the typed
  vocabulary finally has a visual carrier without permanent stage text.
- **Reference behavior:** tldraw arrow labels; Obsidian's edge-less graph
  is the contrast (the cradle is richer and should show it on demand).
- **Landing seam:** `GraphCanvas.tsx` label pass next to the existing
  label collision boxes.
- **UI harmonisation:** label style identical to node captions; default
  view unchanged (labels appear on emphasis only — the stillness law).
- **Acceptance:** hover a typed edge → its kind renders and fades; label
  boxes participate in the existing collision avoidance; no label in
  exports/screenshots unless emphasis was active.

targets.title: The instrument rail, rendered

definition.markdown:
### D1 — The instrument rail, rendered

- **What it does:** the six-tab rail becomes real UI in the cradle —
  switch instrument (lens or cradle surface) from one place, with the
  active tab and geometry already modelled (`instrumentRail.ts:27-60`,
  localStorage key in place, zero consumers today — FINDINGS §1).
- **Reference behavior:** Obsidian's leaf/tab navigation (obsidian-re A1
  workspace lifecycle); Miro's board-switcher quietness (doc-cited).
- **Landing seam:** consumers in `TechneCentre.tsx:87-93` + the cradle
  shell; rail state and hosted-lens state sync both ways (`app.ts:1014`
  lens switch writes the rail).
- **UI harmonisation:** six small tabs in the cradle's own navigation
  grammar; instrument names as written in `instruments.ts:29-36`.
- **Acceptance:** switching Canvas→Timeline→Graph from the rail preserves
  the opened subject's binding (same subject_ref reachable after each
  hop); the localStorage key updates; no second navigation state — the
  hosted lens and the rail never disagree.

targets.title: Saved views carry their subject basis

definition.markdown:
### D2 — Saved views carry their subject basis

- **What it does:** a named view records the subject/binding basis it was
  composed against, so applying it from another binding knows what it is
  looking at — the one-field identity law (TECHNE-DUAL-READING §3) at the
  view level.
- **Reference behavior:** the dead model's CanvasView artifact carried
  subject/reading/snapshot basis (`view.ts:69-72`) — the designed spec.
- **Landing seam:** `ResearchNamedView` gains optional basis fields
  (material record, closed-key validation extended; B4's drift notice
  reads them).
- **UI harmonisation:** invisible until a mismatch: the B4 status
  sentence is the only surface.
- **Acceptance:** save a view under binding X; apply from binding Y with
  the same subject — applies cleanly; apply against a different subject —
  the notice names the basis difference; absent basis (legacy views)
  behaves exactly as today.

definition.markdown:
### D3 — Graph saved views restore the camera

- **What it does:** saved graph views currently restore filters only —
  they gain the camera, so a named view is a place, not just a filter set.
- **Reference behavior:** Obsidian graph filter/groups persistence (A3);
  the cradle's own travel history already persists camera
  (`oi-cradle.knowledge-travel.v1:<binding>`, KnowledgeSurface `:53-66`).
- **Landing seam:** `SavedGraphView {name, filters}` (`filters.ts:136-141`)
  gains camera; restore path in `KnowledgeSurface`.
- **UI harmonisation:** none (existing menu rows).
- **Acceptance:** save a view after travelling; reload; apply — filters
  and camera both restore; old views without camera restore filters only
  (backward-compatible decode).

targets.title: One time model across both halves of M2′

definition.markdown:
### T1 — One time model across both halves of M2′
**What.** The chronology (vendored lens) and the relation field (cradle pure
modules) read one time model: epoch-ms instants carrying the full
precision ladder (millennium→subsecond) and each instant's own UTC offset.
The bridge stops coarsening hour/minute/second/subsecond to "day"
(FINDINGS G1).
**Reference.** vis-timeline runs a single Date-backed axis from milliseconds
to year×1000 (`TimeStep.js:404-470`); the cradle's `scale.ts` already owns
the wider honest ladder — the target is that the mounted instrument uses it.
**Seam.** `vendor/research-canvas/packages/desktop-api/src/techneBundle.ts`
(mapping table l.32-40) + `techneTransport.ts` + `canvas/src/timeline/
instant.ts` — the substrate item model gains a precision-carrying anchor
instead of a year float; `src/techne/m0m5/timeline/scale.ts` stays the
authority.
**UI-harmonisation.** No visual change by itself; sub-day facts become
placeable exactly where the relation field's activity lanes already show
them.
**Acceptance.** A reading with a `second`-precision facet renders at
sub-second zoom on the chronology with its true extent
(`scale.ts:100-108` widening), and `node --test` on the bridge proves
facet precision survives round-trip verbatim (no "day" substitution);
the existing precision honesty tests keep passing.

targets.title: Precision-honest placement and display

definition.markdown:
### T2 — Precision-honest placement and display
**What.** A low-precision fact renders as its honest band, never a point:
millennium → thousand-year band, day → its day (cradle `scale.ts` law),
plus Aeon's documented positioning defaults for display text (unspecified
month → beginning of year, etc.) and **inclusive end dates** rendered
`… – 2016` / `24:00:00` style (T4 merged here as the display convention).
**Reference.** Aeon manual pp. 39-41 ("Event Precision", "How imprecise
events are displayed", end-date inclusivity with `24:00:00`); cradle
`scale.ts:5-11, 100-131` already computes the bands — today nothing draws
them (G2).
**Seam.** `canvas/src/timeline/projection.ts` (`TimelineItem.precision`
already carried at l.15 — dead data), `TimelineNode.tsx` (band rendering),
`ticks.ts` (labels honour precision).
**UI-harmonisation.** Bands use the card's own family styling with a
distinct band fill; no new chrome; label text states precision verbatim
("12th c.", "1963").
**Acceptance.** Fixture reading with one millennium-, one year-, one
day-precision facet: screenshot shows three bands of visibly different
widths each labelled at its precision; band math verified by a pure
function test (band fromMs/toMs equal `expandInstant` output).

Aeon Timeline 2 manual only; installed application unavailable. No source code adoption.

targets.title: Uncertainty presentation (circa, disputed, mythic)

definition.markdown:
### T3 — Uncertainty presentation (circa, disputed, mythic)
**What.** `uncertainty` strings and standing become *visible temporality*:
a fact with `uncertainty: "circa"` or disputed standing renders a hatched/
soft-edged band or badge with the verbatim string on hover; standing
classes come from the existing grammar, never invented per-view.
**Reference.** PeriodO's twin law — the source's textual bound is
authoritative, the structured range only orders and visualises
(`data-model.md:46-62`); `standing.ts:15-25` never upgrades.
**Seam.** Reading already carries it (`contract.ts:220` facet
`uncertainty`; relations carry `standing` → properties at
`researchInstrumentsData.ts:168-173`); seams are `TimelineNode.tsx`
(badge/band), `TimelineRelationshipLayer.tsx` (edge class from standing),
`relationFieldView.tsx` (already renders standing chips — the chronology
catches up to it).
**UI-harmonisation.** One visual vocabulary across both M2′ projections:
the six standing classes and their colours are shared constants, not two
dialects.
**Acceptance.** Fixture with sourced / disputed / mythic / uncertain
facts: each renders its class (screenshot); the tooltip carries the
verbatim standing string; a pure test pins class selection to
`standingOf()` output (no second mapping).

definition.markdown:
### T4 — Deep time without fabrication
**What.** The axis extends beyond JS-Date range for old material
(palaeography, cosmology): year-number positioning (BigYear-style integers)
below −99999 and above +275759, with its own tick ladder (age 10⁶ y,
epoch 10⁷, era 10⁸, eon 10⁹).
**Reference.** TimelineJS3 `TLDate.js:459-489` (`BIG_DATE_SCALES`,
`HUMAN_SCALE_MIN_YEAR`) — one dataset spans human + cosmological time.
**Seam.** `canvas/src/timeline/instant.ts` (a bigint/integer year path
beside the Date path), `scale.ts`/`ticks.ts` (ladder extension), reading
side accepts wide `xsd:gYear`-style years (PeriodO l.58: "any number of
digits"; year 0000 = 1 BCE convention noted).
**UI-harmonisation.** Tier names surface in the existing tier readout
(`TimelineLens.tsx:598`) — "eon", "age" are tier labels, no new panels.
**Acceptance.** A fixture with −780000 and +4.5e9-year facts positions and
ticks correctly (pure test on the year path); human-scale fixtures
unchanged (regression: existing tick tests pass).

targets.title: Relative time for undated work (no fake dates)

definition.markdown:
### T5 — Relative time for undated work (no fake dates)
**What.** A subject's undated but *ordered* material (phases, sessions,
archetypal sequences) can be read on a relative axis — Day 0 / Week 0 /
T+offset from a disclosed zero ref — instead of being excluded or
fabricated into calendar time.
**Reference.** Aeon manual pp. 41-42 (Regular / Weekly / Daily / Time
styles with a configurable zero date); dual-reading TD3: "archetypal or
cultural relation does not become a fake historical date".
**Seam.** `src/techne/m0m5/timeline/scale.ts` (a relative projection
beside the calendar one), `session.ts` (`DisclosureSession` gains the
zero-ref as part of the maintained time window, see S3); the relation
field's phase/activity modes consume it first.
**UI-harmonisation.** The projection switch is the existing Chronology /
Relations row; relative mode appears only when a reading discloses a
warranted zero ref, otherwise honestly absent.
**Acceptance.** Undated facets ordered by sequence render on a relative
axis labelled "Day 0…"; no calendar year appears anywhere in the view;
switching back restores the calendar axis byte-identically.

targets.title: The shared time-axis contract for lane 4 (M4′ World/Places)

definition.markdown:
### T6 — The shared time-axis contract for lane 4 (M4′ World/Places)
**What.** One wire shape both M2′ and M4′ consume — dated events with
uncertainty and provenance on a shared time axis, plus period bands and
the session's time window. Not a new store: a published projection of the
reading the instruments already share.
**Reference.** Chronas: one year cursor drives the map's polity layer
(capture 2026-10-07); `ql.techne/v1` already carries every field needed.
**Shape (all existing contract fields, published as the seam):**
```
techne:time-axis/v1 (projection of a TechneReading — no new truth)
  subject_ref, reading_ref, snapshot_revision   (identity, verbatim)
  events[]: { facet_ref | derived_ref, kind,                 (contract.ts:205-222)
              instant | interval{from,to,precisions}, precision,
              uncertainty?, source_ref?, provenance_selector? (temporalFacets.ts:88) }
  relations[]: { relation_ref|derived, relation, from_ref, to_ref,
                 temporal_facet_ref?, standing?, source_ref? }   (contract.ts:145-158)
  bands[]:   { band_ref, label_verbatim, earliest, latest,       (PeriodO shape, T8)
               source_ref?, note?, editorial_note? }
  window:    { from, to } | null                                  (contract.ts:443)
```
**Seam.** Produced beside `relationFieldState` in
`src/techne/m0m5/timeline/` (pure, node-tested); consumed by the
chronology mount (`researchInstruments.tsx:606-636`) and exposed to the
M4′ surface through the hosted app's existing reading channel
(`host.read`, `TechneCentre.tsx:86`) — lane 4 records this interface
point; lane 2 owns the shape.
**UI-harmonisation.** Both instruments display the same window and the
same event extent; a cursor change in either is a session-window change
(S3), not a local secret.
**Acceptance.** Contract test: the projection validates against
`validateReading` inputs byte-deterministically (same reading → identical
projection, the techneBundle purity law); an integration fixture moves the
window and both projections agree on which events are in scope.

---

definition.markdown:
### T7 — Two-row calendar axis (minor/major labels)
**What.** The axis shows a major label row (year) over a minor row
(month/day/time) that adapts with zoom, with per-scale label formats.
**Reference.** vis-timeline `TimeStep.js` (minor/major `FORMAT` l.909+,
auto-scale ladder, custom format functions l.741-781).
**Seam.** `canvas/src/timeline/TimelineAxis.tsx` + `ticks.ts`
(single-row today); the cradle's `ticksForDomain` (`scale.ts:208-271`)
already computes the ladder — it becomes the tick provider.
**UI-harmonisation.** Axis styling follows the Expressions-family
typographic grammar; labels never animate or reflow between frames.
**Acceptance.** At year zoom the minor row reads months and the major row
years; at day zoom minor reads hours; tick sets equal
`ticksForDomain(...)` output (pure test) and the existing
civil-frame/offset behaviour is preserved (tests exist).

definition.markdown:
### T8 — Periodisation bands (reigns, dynasties, wars, eras)
**What.** Named time bands render behind the events — as axis stripes and
as full-height background lanes — sourced from the reading, with the
source's own label authoritative and earliest/latest used only to draw.
**Reference.** TimelineJS3 eras ("a span of time marked along the edge of
the time slider", `TimeEra.js:9-14`); vis background items
(`component/item/BackgroundItem.js`); PeriodO's period definition is the
data shape; Chronas' era-banded scrubber shows it at historiography
scale.
**Seam.** Reading: temporal facets `kind:"valid"` with labels already
arrive (phasesFromFacets, `relations.ts:389-403`); a `band` reading
surface follows T6's `bands[]`; rendering in the vendored lens's frame
layer (`TimelineSurface.tsx:280-329` archetype band layer becomes the
general band layer).
**UI-harmonisation.** Bands are quiet fills (the audit's stillness law):
never animated, never overlapping event cards, labelled once.
**Acceptance.** Fixture with three sourced bands renders stripes with
verbatim labels; an unsourced band renders with the "authored" standing
class; a band with no position is listed, never drawn (honest absence);
pure tests pin band geometry to the PeriodO-derived earliest/latest.

targets.title: Nested events with zoom-collapsing structure

definition.markdown:
### T9 — Nested events with zoom-collapsing structure
**What.** A parent event (a war, a life, a project) holds child events;
zooming out collapses expanded parents into the parent span, zooming in
expands them; parent extent is computed from children.
**Reference.** Aeon manual pp. 49-53 (multi-level War→Battle→events;
auto-collapse on zoom-out; parent range from children; "Start of X"/"End
of X" preserves a top-down range).
**Seam.** The frame mechanism already does the interaction half
(`frames.ts:59-99`, "Open sub-timeline", "Back to Earth"); the target
adds hierarchy semantics to the reading model (parent_ref on facets or a
composition of relations) and auto-collapse driven by the tier
(`scale.ts`).
**UI-harmonisation.** The breadcrumb stays the frame crumb
(`TimelineLens.tsx:604-617`); expansion is a disclosure act, never
automatic re-layout of unrelated cards.
**Acceptance.** Fixture: war parent + three battles + nine events; at
millennium tier the parent renders as one band; zooming to decade
expands it (screenshot pair); a pure test proves parent fromMs/toMs equal
min(child)/max(child); moving the parent's date moves children (CAS
receipt asserts one native write).

targets.title: Cause and influence chains along the axis

definition.markdown:
### T10 — Cause and influence chains along the axis
**What.** A causal family chain (A —CAUSES→ B —CAUSES→ C) can be walked
*in time*: selecting a chain highlights its edges in sequence, shows each
hop's time offset, and follows it across the camera; undated hops carry
their absence honestly.
**Reference.** Aeon dependencies (manual pp. 46-48: offsets, move-one-
follows) for the interaction; cradle `directedChains` (`relations.ts:
300-329`) already computes chains without inventing chronology.
**Seam.** Relation field mode "cause" (`relationFieldView.tsx:37-39`)
gains the chain walk; the chronology's relationship layer
(`TimelineRelationshipLayer.tsx`) highlights chain members; offsets
computed from the temporal qualifications only when both hops are dated.
**UI-harmonisation.** The chain highlight is the standing-colour
vocabulary at full strength on a dimmed field — a colour journey with
meaning (audit floor #3), no pulsing.
**Acceptance.** Fixture chain with two dated and one undated hop: the
walk shows dated offsets and "no date disclosed" for the undated hop; no
edge is drawn between cards as causal unless its relation type is in the
cause family (`projectionForRelation`); click-to-follow moves the camera
once (no per-frame loads).

targets.title: Standing-aware relation edges on the chronology

definition.markdown:
### T11 — Standing-aware relation edges on the chronology
**What.** Edges on the time axis are styled by the relation's own
standing (sourced/derived/authored/disputed/mythic/unknown) with
direction arrows and a visible legend; the native relation properties
already pushed to the substrate are actually read.
**Reference.** The cradle's own grammar (`standing.ts:83-92` legend) —
the chronology today styles by a fixed type split only (G3,
`TimelineRelationshipLayer.tsx:68-73`).
**Seam.** `TimelineRelationshipLayer.tsx` (class from
`properties.standing` via `standingOf`), plus `relations.ts` edge model
crossing the bridge unchanged.
**UI-harmonisation.** Same legend component as the relation field; the
legend renders whenever edges are shown, on both projections.
**Acceptance.** Fixture with a disputed and a sourced relation between
two dated cards: styles differ, legend lists both, tooltips carry the
verbatim standing; pure test pins edge class selection to `standingOf`.

targets.title: Honest aggregation at broad zoom

definition.markdown:
### T12 — Honest aggregation at broad zoom
**What.** At millennium tier, near-coincident facts compress into honest
count clusters ("7 events, 1601–1650"); clicking a cluster zooms once to
its span; counts are derived, labelled as counts, never drawn as fake
events.
**Reference.** Histography's density histogram (every dot one event,
peaks surface representative events — capture 2026-10-07); vis
ClusterGenerator (`ClusterGenerator.js`) for the interaction; the cradle's
own unused `aggregate()` (`lanes.ts:196-231`) for the honest-count model.
**Seam.** `lanes.ts aggregate()` consumed by the mounted chronology at
tier boundaries; cluster click → `setView` (`timelineStore.ts:202-203`).
**UI-harmonisation.** Clusters render in the category colour of their
members at reduced saturation; the audit's restraint law: no wobble, no
count badge inflation.
**Acceptance.** Fixture with 40 events in one decade renders one cluster
marked 40 at millennium tier; expanding shows all 40 (screenshot pair);
a pure test pins bucket membership to `aggregate()` output; culling still
bounds render cost (existing overscan test style).

targets.title: Scale-window minimap

definition.markdown:
### T13 — Scale-window minimap
**What.** A slim strip over the whole reading domain shows where the
camera window sits; dragging moves the camera, resizing the window zooms —
the whole of time always one glance away.
**Reference.** Histography's bottom bar ("resize the bottom bar to view
any time period or era", capture 2026-10-07).
**Seam.** `TimelineSurface.tsx` (a pure view over `timeExtent` +
`viewState`, both already flowing through it); no new state — the strip
is a projection of the camera the surface already persists.
**UI-harmonisation.** One-line instrument chrome in the family grammar;
hidden at the widest tier when it would duplicate the axis.
**Acceptance.** Dragging the window pans (centre follows); shrinking it
zooms in proportionally; the strip's highlighted extent equals the
`timelineWindowForViewport` computation (pure test); keyboard-only
operation possible (arrow keys as today).

targets.title: Participant spans (lifespans, validity) behind events

definition.markdown:
### T14 — Participant spans (lifespans, validity) behind events
**What.** Participants with validity (a person's birth/death, a place's
identity span, an institution's operation) render as thin spans behind
the event cards of their lane, so events read *against* the span of the
thing that lived them.
**Reference.** Aeon entity birth/death (manual pp. 67, 1720-1725); the
reading model already carries validity facets and place valid_from/to
(`contract.ts:254-255`).
**Seam.** `phasesFromFacets` (`relations.ts:389-403`) + place facets
crossing the bridge; rendering behind cards in the vendored lens's
frame layer (shared with T8 bands, participant-anchored).
**UI-harmonisation.** Participant spans are the quietest element: hairline
fills, label at first occurrence only.
**Acceptance.** Fixture person 1874–1951 with three dated events: the
span renders behind them and clamps honestly if the person's death is
undated (open-ended stays open, no invented end); pure test on span
geometry.

---

targets.title: Named timeline views (the curated view persists)

definition.markdown:
### T15 — Named timeline views (the curated view persists)
**What.** "Save view" on M2′ persists a named view: camera, the active
projection (chronology/relations + relation mode), filters (category,
relation-type, tag), the open sub-timeline frame and the walk position.
Reopening restores the curated state; removing is one act.
**Reference.** The Canvas's own named views (frames + selection +
viewport, `researchMaterial.ts:24, 185-191`) — the timeline reaches
parity with its sibling instrument; Aeon bookmarks (manual p. 67) as the
genre reference.
**Seam.** `researchMaterial.ts` (`oi.research-scene/v1` gains a
`timelineViews` record set beside `namedViews`, same bounds discipline);
`researchInstruments.tsx` M2′ block (the save button exists at l.623 —
it persists only the camera today); `TimelineLens.tsx` filter state
flows into the saved record.
**UI-harmonisation.** Same "Views…" chooser pattern the Canvas studio
uses (`researchInstruments.tsx:435-437`) — one grammar across
instruments.
**Acceptance.** Save with filters + frame + relation mode → reload →
state restored exactly (test IDs: `timeline-filter-*`, `timeline-frame`,
projection toggle all assert their restored state); material validator
accepts and bounds the new record (≤32 views, ref-carrying fields
validated); removing a view never touches semantic records.

targets.title: Card style with a native mapping (the refused write lands)

definition.markdown:
### T16 — Card style with a native mapping (the refused write lands)
**What.** Timeline card colour/style edits persist through a defined
native mapping (per-node presentation in the Scene's research material,
like Canvas card style), instead of today's post-hoc refusal
("Timeline style has no native Scene write mapping yet").
**Reference.** Canvas card-style actions (`researchMaterial.ts:37,
157`) — same treatment, same bounds.
**Seam.** `researchMaterial.ts` `timeline-layout` value gains the style
fields the validator already knows how to bound (colour grammar from
`card-style`); `researchInstruments.tsx:594-600` drops the style
refusal; the mount's load-side join re-applies style
(`researchInstruments.tsx:593`).
**UI-harmonisation.** The colour capability disclosure
(`styleCapability`, `researchInstrumentsData.ts:185`) flips to available
only when the mapping exists — capability honesty preserved either way.
**Acceptance.** Colour an event card → CAS receipt → reload → colour
persisted; `styleCapability.available === true`; a refusal (e.g. budget
exceeded) surfaces in the existing save-error slot with retry
(`TimelineLens.tsx:795-799`), never a silent drop.

targets.title: The session's time window is maintained and consumed

definition.markdown:
### T17 — The session's time window is maintained and consumed
**What.** The DisclosureSession's `time_window` (in the contract since
TB0, never written — G7) is set by M2′ to the window the person is
actually reading, and consumed by `relationFieldState` and by M4′ (T6).
Leaving the instrument records the window; a co-referenced instrument
inherits it.
**Reference.** `state.ts:65-68`'s own law: the window is the session's,
never derived from zoom/pan — so the write is an explicit disclosure act
("Read over this window"), not a camera spy.
**Seam.** `session.ts` `DisclosureSessionGround` gains
`time_window` (validated by `validateSession`, `contract.ts:876-883`);
the M2′ toolbar's explicit set-window act; `relationFieldState(reading,
projection, selection, timeWindow)` already accepts it
(`state.ts:83-98`).
**UI-harmonisation.** One control, in the family grammar, labelled with
the window it will assert; absent until the person sets one (honest
null, `state.ts:66-68`).
**Acceptance.** Set window → `validateSession` passes with
`time_window` present → relation-field availability recomputes against
it (fixture: an event outside the window is reported out-of-scope, not
hidden); crossing instruments preserves the window byte-exact
(`crossCutSession` test extension).

targets.title: Working set and frame persistence (per subject, bounded)

definition.markdown:
### T18 — Working set and frame persistence (per subject, bounded)
**What.** The working-set stack and the open sub-timeline frame persist
with the subject's saved view (T15) as ref-carrying records — a
historian's open exploration survives the session.
**Reference.** The working-set model is already property-complete and
ref-keyed (`timelineStore.ts:29-41`); frames are ref-carrying today but
session-local (`TimelineLens.tsx:116` state).
**Seam.** `researchMaterial.ts` timelineViews record (T15) carries
`workingSetRefs[]`, `frameNodeId?` with the same ≤64-ref bound discipline
as `namedViews.selectedRefs`; the mount rehydrates through
`expandNode` (fresh reads, never stale copies).
**UI-harmonisation.** No new chrome — restoring is part of view
application, with the existing stack UI (`TimelineWorkingSet`).
**Acceptance.** Save view with 3 stacked nodes + frame → reload → stack
rehydrates by ref (fresh `expandNode` reads; a node whose source changed
re-reads at current revision, never renders a stale copy); bounds
enforced by the validator; removing the view removes nothing semantic.

---

targets.title: Evidence-grounded opening (event → source at its anchor)

definition.markdown:
### T19 — Evidence-grounded opening (event → source at its anchor)
**What.** An event card's evidence affordance opens the source at its
exact selector — the kernel's `authored_relation` anchor byte ranges
(`kernel/src/graph.rs:840, 953`) and the reading's provenance selectors
(`temporalFacets.ts:88`) reach the surface, so "show me why this is dated
1874" lands on the passage.
**Reference.** The reading's own selector grammar (`contract.ts:261-265`
`text_span`); the cradle's Reading lens opens material but not at an
offset (FINDINGS §1.6 — G10).
**Seam.** The bridge stops discarding provenance (`techneBundle.ts:66-69`
"no substrate slot" — the slot is T6's `provenance_selector`);
`TimelineNode.tsx` evidence affordance → `host.inspectSubject(ref,
{selector})` → the cradle's source reader scrolls to the anchor.
**UI-harmonisation.** The affordance is the evidence standing colour
itself — the evidence action looks like what it is (audit: metadata
lives in the binding record, surfaced on request, never painted on the
stage).
**Acceptance.** Fixture reading with a `text_span` selector: opening the
evidence shows the source scrolled/selected at start–end; a facet with
no selector shows the honest absence (control present only when a
selector exists); the subject_ref/revision ride unchanged (identity
law).

targets.title: Cross-instrument carry to the globe (the lane-4 handoff)

definition.markdown:
### T21 — Cross-instrument carry to the globe (the lane-4 handoff)
**What.** Selecting an event (or setting the window, T17) while M4′ is
open moves the globe to that event's place and year; selecting a place in
M4′ focuses M2′ on its span. Both read T6's one projection; neither
copies data.
**Reference.** Chronas: the year cursor drives the map layer (capture
2026-10-07); TD5's `OCCURRED_AT/LOCATED_AT` vocabulary (`walk.ts:24-33`
already resolves place for events).
**Seam.** T6's `techne:time-axis/v1` + the session window (T17); the
hosted app's instrument bridge posts `{graphNodeId, window}` through the
existing host-command grammar (`hostedApp.ts` postMessage channel).
**UI-harmonisation.** Each instrument keeps its native controls (dual
reading §7 UI); the carry is a change of the shared session state, never
a duplicated cursor widget.
**Acceptance.** Integration fixture: select event with LOCATED_AT place
→ M4′ camera arrives at that place and year (one hop, one message);
select place in M4′ → M2′ frames that place's sub-timeline (existing
`setFrameForNode`); a place-less event carries the window only, with the
honest "no location disclosed" state.

targets.title: Identity-honest instrument handoff (the disclosure contract)

definition.markdown:
### T22 — Identity-honest instrument handoff (the disclosure contract)
**What.** Every handoff in or out of M2′ (rail switch, cut crossing,
subject refresh) preserves the identity bundle — subject_ref, whole/relation
refs, source + revision basis, occasion ref, selection standing — and
M2′ reports its temporal facet truthfully ("No dates disclosed by this
source" already exists; the target pins the full bundle).
**Reference.** `crossCutSession` (`contract.ts:918-941`) and
`session.ts:140-159` already implement the law; the target closes the
gap between the contract and the mounted instrument's local state (which
today keys views per subject but discloses nothing about what survived).
**Seam.** `session.ts` + `researchInstruments.tsx` `stateFor(key)`
(l.286, already per-subject); a disclosure readout in the family's
status line ("subject X · reading basis rN · window W").
**UI-harmonisation.** The status line is the instrument's existing
message slot (`researchInstruments.tsx:238`) — one line, plain text.
**Acceptance.** Contract tests: crossing with a drifted session refuses
and leaves state untouched; a successful handoff's navigation hop
records from/to/selection_ref; the status line renders the exact
subject_ref and revision basis (plain-language law).

---

### T24 — Focus mode and fullscreen for the stage
**What.** M2′ gains the audit's floor: real fullscreen (the stage owns
the screen) and a focus mode that hides all chrome but the axis and
cards, keyed `F`, restoring on escape — the working set and walk panels
are revealable, not permanent furniture.

(`requestFullscreen`, focus mode, key F).

portals exist); identical implementation to the expression.html floor so
the grammar is one grammar.
**Acceptance.** `F` toggles a chrome-hidden state (screenshot pair);
fullscreen requests and exits cleanly (API call verified in the
mount); state restores exactly on exit; keyboard map documented in the
control's title text.

targets.title: Capability honesty as the instrument's voice

definition.markdown:
### T25 — Capability honesty as the instrument's voice
**What.** Every absence keeps its honest sentence and gains its positive
twin: "No dates disclosed by this source" (exists), "no temporal facets
and no dated relations are disclosed — nothing is placed on a time axis,
and none is invented" (`relations.ts:277`), the unavailable-mode reasons,
the standing legend — all rendered from the same availability data, in
plain language, with zero fabricated placeholders.
**Reference.** The existing discipline is already the bar (`TimelineLens
empty state`, `projectionAvailability`, `styleCapability` refusal);
the target is one shared availability voice, not four dialects.
**Seam.** A shared availability/legend render helper consumed by the
chronology toolbar, the relation-field mode bar, and the M2′ status
line.
**Acceptance.** Fixture readings covering: no temporal facets (empty
state + reasons), temporal facets but no relations (timeline only,
relations modes disabled with reasons), relations but no dates
(relation field only, chronology honest-empty). Screenshot set; every
unavailable control carries its reason verbatim (aria-label/title
asserts).

targets.title: The journey timeline surface

definition.markdown:
- **E01 The journey timeline surface.** A time-proportional track for the
  whole expression: one clip per scene, width ∝ `duration`, the playhead
  running on global time, the scene strip (`renderTimeline`,
  `app.ts:221`) becoming its collapsed form.
  *Reference behavior:* every surveyed editor renders clips on a
  time-proportional track over a global clock — Blender's sequencer
  channels (`DNA_sequence_types.h:360-476`), Kdenlive's
  `TimelineModel`/track/clip composition (`timelinemodel.hpp:41-52`).
  *Mapping:* the track is the document's `scenes[]`; clip extents derive
  from `expressionTiming` — no new time object is invented (Σ durations
  stays the law; a global time base would be a second clock).
  *Landing seam:* replace the timeline panel body in
  `field-studies-journeys/src/app.ts` (`renderTimeline` `:221`); playhead
  keeps its id (`expression-playhead`) so `app.ts:849`'s UI tick is
  untouched; edit gestures route through `store.change`.
  *UI harmonisation:* same rail language as the existing strip
  (thumbnails, save-state dots); keyboard: Space = play/pause (existing),
  Left/Right = step; the panel remains collapsible to today's strip.
  *Acceptance:* screenshot of a 5-scene expression with visibly unequal
  clip widths matching durations (G6); playhead at global t maps to the
  same scene+local-time that `expressionTiming` reports (property assert);
  drag on a clip edge is E05.

targets.title: Scene-as-clip: content vs timeline coordinates

definition.markdown:
- **E02 Scene-as-clip: content vs timeline coordinates.** Adopt the
  strip discipline: a Scene's **content identity** (`scene_ref`) is
  stable under every timeline move; its **timeline facts** (order,
  `duration`, `transition`) are mutable addressable state. Editing acts
  never mutate content to move a clip.
  *Reference behavior:* Blender `Strip` carries `start`/`len` with
  `startofs/endofs` handles and `anim_startofs/endofs` media trim
  separated from content (`DNA_sequence_types.h:360-476`); Kdenlive ids
  "have nothing to do with Melt IDs" — model ids stable under all moves
  (`timelinemodel.hpp:44-46`).
  *Mapping:* `scene_ref` ≈ content id; `scenes[]` order ≈ `start`;
  `duration` ≈ `len`. The Scene's living field is the "media" — it has
  no intrinsic length, so no media-trim handles exist (honest divergence:
  a scene shows its whole content; what trims is when it yields the
  stage).
  *Landing seam:* model-level invariant in `model.ts`/`sceneWorkflow.ts`
  (timeline ops reorder/retime but never touch content fields);
  kernel-side `scene_reorder` already carries `scene_refs` — identity is
  preserved by construction (`expression/types.ts:52`).
  *UI harmonisation:* clip chrome (name, save-state dot) persists across
  moves — visual continuity of identity.
  *Acceptance:* property test — after reorder/retime/split sequences,
  every surviving `scene_ref` maps to a scene whose field/entities
  digest equals its pre-move digest; one screenshot showing a moved clip
  retaining its thumbnail and dot (G6).

  index becomes a derived view, never the address. Kills the audit's

  not positions (`timelinemodel.hpp:44-52`); Blender RNA paths name
  strips, not slots.

  `scene_reorder`); the app's `Scene.id` view labels already map 1:1
  through `SceneBinding` (`kernelDocumentBridge.ts:117,247`).
  *Landing seam:* `app.ts:300` (`setScene(index)` → overload accepting
  ref with index resolved internally); the `__FIELD_STUDIES__.setScene`
  disclosure (`app.ts:963`) becomes ref-typed (index accepted for
  compatibility, announced); `jumpToScene` (`app.ts:1055`) loses its
  index re-derivation; site host already passes sceneId + sceneMap
  (`site/src/expression/ExpressionApp.tsx:193-198`) — align the
  disclosure to it.

  *Acceptance:* scripted: reorder scenes, then `setScene(<ref of scene
  now in another position>)` opens the right scene; `?scene=<ref>` deep
  link opens by ref on the site page and in the app (see E22).

targets.title: Insert vs overwrite move semantics; gaps are still scenes

definition.markdown:
- **E04 Insert vs overwrite move semantics; gaps are still scenes.** The
  array is the ripple law: scenes are contiguous, so "ripple" =
  insert/remove shifting successors, and "overwrite" = replace in place.
  A timed void is authored as a **still scene**, not a null gap — the
  audit's stillness floor made literal in the data model (G2).
  *Reference behavior:* Kdenlive `requestClipMove` with group/ripple
  semantics and ripple resize (`timelinecontroller.h:662-665`);
  Blender's explicit gap removal as a separate act
  (`SEQ_edit.hh:69-80`) — oi.journey's contiguous array is the honest
  simplification (a scene is always "there"), so gap tools are not
  ported; instead a **slate/still scene starter** exists.
  *Mapping:* insert = `scene_create` + `scene_reorder`; overwrite =
  `scene_remove` + `scene_create` composite; still scene = `scene_create`
  with a quiet presentation (low count, no automation — authoring starter,
  not a new kind).
  *Landing seam:* `reorderScene` (`app.ts:468`) generalises to the two
  move modes; scene-add menu gains the still-scene starter.
  *UI harmonisation:* drag affordance shows insert edge (line) vs
  overwrite (highlight) — same visual grammar as the entity drag ghost.
  *Acceptance:* insert between scenes 2/3 leaves 1-2 **A** 3-4 →
  1-2-A-3-4 with durations summing identically (receipt: `scene_reorder`
  listing all `scene_refs`); still scene plays as deliberate stillness
  (G2 screenshot), not a dropped frame rate.

  (E15); clamp at 1 s/3600 s surfaced as named refusal, not silent snap.

targets.title: Split scene at the playhead

definition.markdown:
- **E07 Split scene at the playhead.** Cut one scene into two at global
  time t: left keeps content with tracks/sequence split at local time,
  right gets the same content re-based; durations sum to the original;
  crossfade between them defaults to 0 (a true cut) — author's choice.
  *Reference behavior:* Blender `SEQ_edit.hh` split with SOFT/HOLD
  methods (`SEQ_edit.hh:49-67`); Shotcut `SplitCommand` as one named
  undo unit (`timelinecommands.h:484`).
  *Mapping:* atomic composite over existing grammar: `scene_create` (new
  ref) + two `scene_material_set`s + `scene_reorder` — expressible
  **today**; must be receipted as ONE composite (E16), never three
  floating edits.
  *Landing seam:* new op beside `reorderScene` (`app.ts:468`); splitting
  walks `propertyTracks` points (points at < t stay, ≥ t re-based) and
  entity sequences (step boundary chosen at or before t — a sequence step
  is atomic; named limitation).
  *UI harmonisation:* the playhead gains the universal split affordance
  (blade icon in the timeline's tool row); key S.
  *Acceptance:* track value evaluated at t−ε on the left scene equals
  evaluation at the right scene's local ε (continuity assert; golden
  values per E08); one undo restores the unsplit scene and its ref
  disappears from the kernel document (receipt chain visible).

targets.title: Interpolation types on property tracks

definition.markdown:
- **E08 Interpolation types on property tracks.** Per-keyframe-pair
  interpolation beyond linear: `hold` (constant), `smooth` (smoothstep),
  `bezier` (with E09 handles); absent type = linear (byte-compatible with
  every existing document).
  *Reference behavior:* Olive `kLinear|kHold|kBezier`
  (`app/node/keyframe.h:46-48`); libopenshot
  `BEZIER|LINEAR|CONSTANT` + AUTO/MANUAL handles (`src/Point.h:29-43`);
  benchmark evidence that keyframe curves are callable at frame rate
  (`doc/JSON-KEYFRAME-BENCHMARK.md`).
  *Mapping:* `PropertyTrack.points` gains an optional per-point type +
  control points; tracks travel whole inside the scene presentation
  envelope, so this is app-model + validation only — the kernel stores
  the envelope verbatim (`kernelExpressions.ts:133-136`).
  *Landing seam:* `propertyTracks.ts:6` (`valueAt`) gains the
  interpolators; `validateTracks` (`:5`) validates types/monotonic time
  (existing law kept).
  *UI harmonisation:* curve lanes render in the E01 timeline's channel
  area with the stage's own palette discipline (G3: tint curves visibly
  move colour).
  *Acceptance:* golden-value tests — linear equals today's `valueAt`
  bit-for-bit on legacy data; hold/step, smoothstep and a canonical
  bezier evaluated at fixed samples; a rendered colour-journey scene
  (G3, G6) whose background/palette ride bezier tracks.

targets.title: Channel discipline

definition.markdown:
- **E10 Channel discipline.** Per-channel solo/mute/visibility over the
  existing addressable-path law — the whitelist
  (`field.params.*`, `entity.position/scale/tintWeight/force/sequence.*`,
  `propertyTracks.ts:4`) is **kept**: solo/mute are evaluation-time
  state, never new address space.
  *Reference behavior:* Kdenlive `GroupsModel` (selection acts on
  related members coherently, `groupsmodel.hpp:18-24`) as the model for
  grouping; standard channel-solo semantics of every NLE.
  *Mapping:* presentation-only state in the working view (not yet a
  kernel field); honest note: solo/mute do not travel in saved documents
  until the owner commissions that — drafts may keep them
  (renderer-local, like camera snap).
  *Landing seam:* `evaluateTracks` (`propertyTracks.ts:8`) filters by
  channel state; channel list UI feeds from existing tracks.
  *UI harmonisation:* channel rows adopt the automation lane row
  language already in the app (`automationEditor.ts`).
  *Acceptance:* soloing one colour channel while others animate → only
  it moves (paired screenshots, G5); saved draft omits solo/mute state;
  reload changes nothing about document contents (digest equal).

targets.title: Typed, parameterised transitions

definition.markdown:
- **E11 Typed, parameterised transitions.** The single hard-coded
  crossfade (`actTransition`, `app.ts:76-82`) becomes a typed transition
  per seam: `cut`, `crossfade`, `dip-to-colour` (through the scene's own
  background — the colour journey made structural, G3), `wipe` — each
  with the seam's existing `transition` duration and, for dip/wipe, a
  small parameter set. The chain-easing set already validated
  (`smoothstep|linear|kineticSnap|whip`, `app.ts:82`) stays the easing
  vocabulary.
  *Reference behavior:* MLT's service ontology treats a transition as a
  first-class attached service with properties
  (`mlt/src/framework/mlt_types.h:292`, `mlt.h:53-69`); Kdenlive
  compositions are model objects with their own move/insert requests
  (`requestCompositionMove`, `timelinemodel.hpp:463-465`).
  *Mapping:* a per-scene `transitionKind` + params inside the scene
  presentation envelope (travel whole via `scene_material_set`) — no new
  Change kind; the number `transition` stays the duration.
  *Landing seam:* `actTransition` (`app.ts:76-82`) and the
  `setScene` crossfade path (`app.ts:301`) gain the type switch; the
  capture recorder must honour it (it already frames transitions,
  `app.ts:849`).
  *UI harmonisation:* transition type chosen from the timeline seam
  gutter (small glyph between clips — same icon language as the tool
  rail); inspector shows the same control with numeric params.
  *Acceptance:* four named screenshots (one per type, G6) at mid-
  transition; dip-to-colour lands exactly on `field.background` (pixel
  check, G5); capture of a transition renders the same type.

targets.title: Journey markers

definition.markdown:
- **E12 Journey markers.** Named, coloured time points on the sequence:
  create at playhead, rename, move, jump next/previous; markers are
  authoring/navigation furniture — never stage content (G1: metadata
  stays off the stage).
  *Reference behavior:* Kdenlive guide/marker models with snap
  integration (`snapmodel.hpp` feeds guides); Shotcut `MarkersModel`
  with ripple options (`timelinecommands.h:104-138`).
  *Mapping:* **the set's one genuinely new kernel surface**, named
  honestly: either (a) a `markers` field on the journey-level
  presentation (`oi.journey-properties/v1`, already the carrier for
  description/loop/shared — `kernelDocumentBridge.ts:251`), travelling
  through `scene_material_set`-style whole-envelope writes, or (b) a new
  `marker_set` Change kind. Recommendation: (a) first (no grammar
  change), promote to (b) if marker edits need their own receipts.
  Owner-decision flag on (b).
  *Landing seam:* marker store in the journey presentation; UI in the
  E01 ruler; `?marker=<ref>` deep link (E22).
  *UI harmonisation:* marker glyphs reuse the guide colour discipline;
  marker list lives in the existing timeline panel, not a new surface.
  *Acceptance:* create/rename/move each produce a visible receipt (or
  the documented envelope-write) and one undo; next/prev jumps land
  exactly (playhead assert); markers never render on the stage (G1).

targets.title: In/out loop regions

definition.markdown:
- **E13 In/out loop regions.** Transport plays/loops between an in and
  out point; the journey `loop` flag remains the whole-journal case.
  A region looping over a still scene is a lawful reading mode (G2 —
  stillness is authored, and repeatable).
  *Reference behavior:* universal NLE in/out + loop; Kdenlive zone
  handling in guides; the existing `automationLoop` pattern
  (`app.ts:118-120`) shows the app's loop idiom.
  *Mapping:* in/out are presentation-level working state (like markers,
  E12 option (a)); `loop` stays kernel-carried.
  *Landing seam:* transport section of the timeline (E01);
  `sceneElapsed`/`journeyPlaying` clock (`app.ts:844`) honours the
  region bounds.
  *UI harmonisation:* region bracket renders in the timeline ruler;
  keyboard: I/O set/clear, matching the app's single-key law.
  *Acceptance:* play with region [a,b) wraps exactly at b→a (clock
  assert); loop over a still scene renders a held frame with no churn
  (G2 screenshot); clearing the region restores whole-journey behavior.

targets.title: Nested expression occurrence

definition.markdown:
- **E14 Nested expression occurrence.** Place another expression into a
  scene as a bounded occurrence (the meta-strip / nested-sequence move):
  it plays inside the host scene's timing and stays addressable by its
  own `expression_ref`.
  *Reference behavior:* Blender meta-strips are real nesting — a
  `seqbase` list inside a strip (`DNA_sequence_types.h:420`), editable
  in place or opened solo.
  *Mapping:* the kernel already holds the substrate: the **reuse
  register** (`reuse_set`/`reuse_clear`, `expression/types.ts:69-70`;
  disclosed budgets `expression.rs:910`). The target is the editor
  affordance over it: place/resize/remove a reuse occurrence, and the
  renderer evaluating it within the host scene's budget (pages/limits
  per `kernelDocumentBridge.ts:185-201` discipline — a nested field must
  respect the resident renderer budget, refusing honestly if over).
  *Landing seam:* scene-add menu gains "place expression…"; kernel
  round-trips the `reuse_set` change.
  *UI harmonisation:* nested occurrences get a distinct clip/entity
  sheen (same visual family as native-scene badges).
  *Acceptance:* a nested expression placed in a host scene plays within
  host duration (screen capture, G6); its `expression_ref` appears in
  the kernel document's reuse record; removing it receipts
  `reuse_clear` and restores budget.

targets.title: Labelled undo/redo converging with kernel act history

definition.markdown:
- **E15 Labelled undo/redo converging with kernel act history.** Undo
  stops being anonymous full-document clones (`store.ts:7-18`, cap 60,
  no labels): each undo entry carries the operation name and the kernel
  changes it produced; undo/redo at or above the last kernel save
  re-issues **compensating kernel changes** (the same grammar, inverted)
  so the kernel revision history and the editor's undo stack describe
  the same work.
  *Reference behavior:* Kdenlive's design law — every elementary change
  writes its own inverse as it executes; composites get undo/redo pairs
  for free and a failing step cancels what was done
  (`timelinemodel.hpp:49-52`); Shotcut's named QUndoCommands
  (`MoveClipCommand` `timelinecommands.h:319`, `SplitCommand` `:484`).
  *Mapping:* the kernel side already receipts: `edit` carries
  `expected_revision` and returns the new revision
  (`kernelExpressions.ts:244-247`); durable act records exist
  (`oi.expression-act/v1`, `expression_act_store.rs:1-33` — replayable,
  archived, never deleted). The editor attaches the change list to each
  undo entry and, when the document is kernel-hosted, derives the
  compensating change set from it (parameter_set for value flips,
  scene_reorder for moves, and so on — the grammar is invertible for
  everything the app emits after E20).
  *Landing seam:* `store.ts` entries gain `{label, changes?}`; save
  path (`kernelExpressions.ts:238-249`) records which entries are
  kernel-clean.
  *UI harmonisation:* undo labels appear in the existing undo affordance
  (and toast on revert), phrased in the app's own voice ("Trim scene 3",
  "Reorder scenes").
  *Acceptance:* after an edit→save→undo sequence, the kernel document
  digest equals the pre-edit digest (receipted round-trip); the undo
  stack shows human labels; an act record for the edit is inspectable
  by ref (receipt evidence).

targets.title: Atomic composite edits

definition.markdown:
- **E16 Atomic composite edits.** Multi-step gestures (E06 roll, E07
  split, E04 overwrite) are one transaction: either all changes apply or
  none; a mid-gesture failure reverts what was applied and leaves **no**
  undo entry.
  *Reference behavior:* Kdenlive: "if an operation fails for some
  reason, we can easily cancel the steps that have been done so far
  without corrupting anything" (`timelinemodel.hpp:49-51`).
  *Mapping:* the app store already has the transaction idiom
  (`begin/finish/change` with baseline restore on throw,
  `store.ts:12-18`) — the target extends it to kernel batches: a
  composite's change list is submitted as one `edit` (one
  `expected_revision`, one receipt), so the kernel never holds a
  half-composite.
  *Landing seam:* `store.change` batching + the single-edit submission
  in `saveKernelExpression` (`kernelExpressions.ts:238-249`) — no code
  path may split one gesture across revisions.
  *UI harmonisation:* none visible; a failed composite surfaces the
  existing toast/refusal grammar.
  *Acceptance:* injected failure mid-split leaves document byte-equal
  (digest assert), zero undo entries, kernel revision unchanged; the
  happy path produces exactly one revision increment per gesture.

targets.title: Autosave schedule attaining the A1 shape

definition.markdown:
- **E17 Autosave schedule attaining the A1 shape.** Keep the working
  draft safety net, but adopt the schedule the Obsidian A1 study
  costed and the cradle accepted as precedent: trailing-debounce
  autosave, **immediate save on context switches** (scene change, panel
  close, open/save commands), and **flush-on-quit with grace**
  (recreation-backlog T2, `recreation-backlog.md:46-55`; the D-1 posture
  discipline, `:13-21`). Today's 350 ms single debounce (`app.ts:144`)
  plus the 5 s library throttle (`app.ts:159`) becomes: draft debounce
  (unchanged 350 ms coalescing), immediate draft flush on
  `setScene`/rail switch/studio close/beforeunload.
  *Reference behavior:* Obsidian 1.7.7 A1: 2 s trailing autosave +
  immediate on command/leaf-switch + flush-on-quit with grace —
  measured, gate-proven classes (recreation-backlog T2).
  *Mapping:* pure schedule change over the existing recovery owners
  (`recovery.ts:55-56` native-first, IndexedDB, localStorage fallback
  order preserved; never a silent browser fallback after native failure
  — `kernelExpressions.ts:71-81` law kept).
  *Landing seam:* `flushDraft`/`markSaved` (`app.ts:140-172`) gain
  flush triggers; no storage-shape change (that is E18).
  *UI harmonisation:* save-status line keeps its existing voice
  ("Working copy backed up on this device" etc., `app.ts:155-157`).
  *Acceptance:* kill the host mid-edit after a context switch → relaunch
  recovers to the last context switch, not the last 350 ms window
  (scripted crash test); beforeunload flush verified by pending-write
  counter reaching zero.

targets.title: Atomic, per-document storage; corruption quarantine

definition.markdown:
- **E18 Atomic, per-document storage; corruption quarantine.** The
  standalone library stops being one JSON array written wholesale on
  every save (`store.ts:34` — O(library) per write, one torn write loses
  the library): per-document keys + a manifest, each write atomic
  (IndexedDB keys are atomic; the localStorage fallback mirrors the same
  per-key shape). Unreadable entries are **quarantined verbatim, never
  dropped** — the existing law (`store.ts:29-33`) kept and per-key.
  *Reference behavior:* the kernel's own store discipline
  (`expression_act_store.rs:7-12`: atomic replace = temp + fsync +
  rename, CAS revisions); Shotcut's dedicated autosave-file object
  (`AutoSaveFile : public QFile`, `autosavefile.h:27`).
  *Mapping:* **D-1 decision point, restated for this lane** — Obsidian
  writes in place, non-atomic; the D-1 posture chose atomic-by-default
  with a documented divergence note, chosen once and never mixed
  (`recreation-backlog.md:13-21`). This target adopts that posture:
  atomic per-document writes, divergence note "no single-file vault
  compatibility to preserve" (the library is app-local, not an
  interchange format).
  *Landing seam:* `store.ts` (library) + `recovery.ts` draft stores;
  migration: existing array library read once, split per-document, array
  retained read-only one release, then quarantined.
  *UI harmonisation:* none; failure voice unchanged ("Existing library
  could not be read. It has not been overwritten.").
  *Acceptance:* corrupt one document key → others load, the bad key is
  listed in `readLibraryDetailed().errors` and preserved byte-verbatim
  (existing contract, now per-key); torn-write simulation (partial
  write) never loses a *different* document.

targets.title: Crash recovery: draft vs last kernel save

definition.markdown:
- **E19 Crash recovery: draft vs last kernel save.** After an unclean
  exit, reopening a hosted expression offers the real choice: resume the
  draft, or open the kernel's last saved revision — with a visible diff
  (scenes/durations/params changed) — instead of silently resuming or
  silently losing the draft.
  *Reference behavior:* Kdenlive's crash-backup flow
  (`backupwidget.*`, `temporarydata.*` in `src/project/dialogs/`): the
  reopen path surfaces recovered temporaries as a first-class decision.
  *Mapping:* the kernel holds the authoritative revision
  (`expression_ref` + `revision`); drafts live in the recovery owners
  (`recovery.ts:55-56`); both already exist — the target is the
  comparison surface and the explicit choice.
  *Landing seam:* boot path where `readDraft` finds a draft newer than
  the kernel document's `updatedAt`/revision (hosted mode); diff walks
  `sceneParameterChanges` (`sceneWorkflow.ts:27-35`) — it exists.
  *UI harmonisation:* the dialog uses the confirm-dialog grammar
  (`app.ts:616`); shows per-scene save-state dots (existing visual).
  *Acceptance:* scripted crash after N kernel-saved + M draft edits →
  reopen presents both; choosing kernel revision discards the draft
  *to quarantine* (recoverable, not deleted); choosing draft opens with
  draft contents and a pending save diff.

targets.title: Save expressibility: emit the kernel's whole standing Change grammar

definition.markdown:
- **E20 Save expressibility: emit the kernel's whole standing Change
  grammar.** The app's diff refuses things the kernel can express:
  retitle, scene removal, parameter removal, automation edits, subject
  edits all die as "not expressible as a kernel edit in this cut"
  (`kernelExpressions.ts:156-204`) while the kernel grammar has `rename`,
  `scene_remove`, `scene_reorder`, `scene_create`, `parameter_set` and
  more (`expression/types.ts:39-72`). Target: `documentToChanges` emits
  the existing grammar for every operation the editor can perform, so
  save = receipted changes for the full editing surface; refusals shrink
  to genuinely-unrepresentable cases (and name them).
  *Reference behavior:* the grammar itself is the reference — the gap
  is app-side, not kernel-side (FINDINGS §4, "the gap that matters").
  *Mapping:* direct; `scene_reorder`/`scene_remove`/`rename` land as
  receipts when E01–E07 gestures commit; entity membership stays with
  native Scene operations per the bridge law
  (`kernelViewToChanges`, `kernelDocumentBridge.ts:259-262` — unchanged).
  *Landing seam:* `kernelExpressions.ts:152-232` only.
  *UI harmonisation:* the "not expressible in this cut" toasts become
  the exception, not the everyday.
  *Acceptance:* scripted session performing rename + scene remove +
  scene reorder + parameter edit saves in one `edit`, revision+1, all
  four receipted; the refusal set shrinks to documented cases (list
  them in the gate output).

targets.title: Scene→source→subject chain, with back-references

definition.markdown:
- **E21 Scene→source→subject chain, with back-references.** From any
  bound entity occurrence: reveal its **source** (exists:
  `open`→`summon`, `app.ts:1052`) and its **subject** (the
  `subject_ref`'s owning register reading — the projection side exists,
  `wikiExpression.ts:424-461`), and from a subject, the reverse query:
  where does this subject stand on stage (which scenes/expressions carry
  occurrences of it) — jumpable. This is the one-field identity law
  (dual-reading §3) given an editor affordance.
  *Reference behavior:* Resolve-class media identity (every timeline
  instance traceable to its source bin item) — documentation-only
  possession, named as bar not evidence; the implementable reference is
  the app's own binding spine (`OccurrenceBinding`,
  `kernelDocumentBridge.ts:116,247`; view ids reversible, collisions
  refused, `:134-151`).
  *Mapping:* occurrences already carry `subject` clones
  (`kernelDocumentBridge.ts:247`); the back-reference is a query over
  the opened document's bindings + the register projection
  (`wikiProjectionStore.ts:1-30` — one projection state, many
  apertures; the back-reference MUST go through it, not a second
  index).
  *Landing seam:* inspector context menu on a selected occurrence
  (existing context-panel grammar); back-reference panel in the Library
  rail; `focus` kernel change (exists, `expression/types.ts:57`)
  receipts the jump when hosted.
  *UI harmonisation:* one "reveal" affordance family for source, subject
  and occurrences — same menu, same icons, no per-invention chrome.
  *Acceptance:* from a projected wiki entity: one gesture opens the wiki
  subject at its ref; the back-reference lists exactly the scenes
  carrying it (assert against bindings); each jump receipts a `focus`
  (kernel-hosted) and is undoable (E15).

  (hosted), `?scene=<scene_ref>`, `?marker=<ref>` (E12), `?subject=`
  (E21) — every deep link resolves through the binding spine; positional
  indices are accepted only as deprecated compat and announced.

  passes sceneMap by id (`site/src/expression/ExpressionApp.tsx:193-198`);
  the app README records the `?journey`/`?scene` idiom
  (`expressions-app/README.md:74-78`).

  a fresh client (two-client check); a stale ref (scene removed) opens
  the expression at its start scene with a named note, never a silent

targets.title: Transport: scrub, shuttle, frame stepping

definition.markdown:
- **E24 Transport: scrub, shuttle, frame stepping.** The playhead stops
  being the only clock surface: scrubbing (drag with live field
  evaluation — exists partially via `trackPreview`, `app.ts:710`), JKL
  shuttle (back/pause/forward with speed ramp), and frame stepping;
  the auto-advance clock (`app.ts:844`) becomes one transport mode
  under the same transport state, not the de-facto master.
  *Reference behavior:* JKL shuttle is the professional standard
  (Resolve bar, documentation-only) and present in the open sources'
  transport layers; the honest implementable reference is Kdenlive's
  transport/monitor separation — the *model* separates transport state
  from document state.
  *Mapping:* transport state is working-view state (the recovery
  session already carries `transport` — `recovery.ts:8` — so it
  survives reloads); documents unchanged.
  *Landing seam:* keymap beside the existing shortcuts
  (`app.ts:747-749`); transport UI in the E01 timeline.
  *UI harmonisation:* J/K/L and arrow semantics identical in app,
  site page and in-reader frame.
  *Acceptance:* J/L shuttle ramps and returns to prior state on K
  (state assert); stepping holds exactly one evaluation step; scrub
  audiolessly re-evaluates tracks at pointer rate without advancing
  `simTime` physics (existing scrub law, `app.ts:710`).

definition.markdown:
- **E25 Timeline snap model.** Snap points with candidate ranking and
  navigation: scene boundaries, markers (E12), playhead, in/out (E13),
  keyframe times (E09). Next/previous-snap navigation from the playhead.
  *Reference behavior:* Kdenlive `SnapModel` — add/remove points,
  closest, `getNextPoint`, `getPreviousPoint`
  (`snapmodel.hpp:15-49`) — the exact shape to mirror.
  *Mapping:* pure working-view model (no document surface); candidates
  derive from document state.
  *Landing seam:* replaces the single `camera.snap` toggle's timeline
  counterpart (`app.ts:527` keeps the camera's own snap); S toggles
  timeline snapping; Alt disables momentarily (standard grammar).

  (`drawGuides`, `app.ts:810`).

  neighbour boundary and to markers (order: nearest candidate wins —
  Kdenlive's closest-point law); S toggles; next/prev jumps playhead
  point-to-point (assert).

(PsychogeographicMap.tsx:75-77) to carry `pitch` and `bearing`; enable the
maplibre equivalents (`setPitch` d.ts:11323, `setBearing` d.ts:11315,
`dragRotate` d.ts:12208). Reference: Google Earth's ctrl-drag tilt/rotate
feel; MapLibre camera API (possessed). Seam: SURFACE (renderer view state)
+ MATERIAL (the saved `place` viewport record gains pitch/bearing with
backward-compatible defaults 0). Harmonisation: the instrument keeps its
native camera controls; pitch/bearing indicators join the map's own chrome,
not the shell's. Acceptance: a driven run shows a tilted, rotated globe;
reload restores the saved viewport including pitch/bearing; flat mode
ignores pitch without error. Evidence: maplibre state + saved material
round-trip.

targets.title: Fly-to choreography (`flyToPlace`)

definition.markdown:
**T2 — Fly-to choreography (`flyToPlace`).**
What: `flyToPlace(place_ref | subject_ref)` — an animated camera flight to
a facet, with zoom chosen by the facet's own precision (exact → street
scale, approximate → city, region → continent-scale frame, unlocated → no
flight, the register slot is named instead). Reference: Cesium
`Camera.prototype.flyTo` / `flyToBoundingSphere` (Camera.js:3427, 3662)
for the eased arc and duration-by-distance shape; Google Earth
search-and-fly. Seam: SURFACE (host helper over maplibre `flyTo`,
d.ts:11417); MODELS: zoom-from-precision is derived by
`precisionMarker`'s vocabulary (project.ts:75-86), never re-hard-coded.
Harmonisation: one flight feel shared with the Canvas's `flyToNode`
(researchInstruments.tsx:386) — same easing family. Acceptance: calling
fly-to on each precision class lands at the documented zoom band; an
unlocated place never flies. Evidence: driven run screenshots/state dumps
per class.

targets.title: Layered basemap with an honest offline core

definition.markdown:
**T4 — Layered basemap with an honest offline core.**
What: a layer STACK, not a single source: the bundled offline pack remains
the default ground; explicit opt-in live raster tile sources (satellite /
street / hybrid families) stack above it via the existing
`LiveServicePolicy` "tile_refresh" gate (PsychogeographicMap.tsx:111;
geography/src/policy.ts), with a per-source attribution line rendered on
the map. Reference: Google Earth's imagery + QGIS layer tree semantics;
MapLibre raster sources (`RasterSourceSpecification`, d.ts:4) and the
style's existing raster branch (mapStyle.ts:87-91). Seam: SURFACE
(mapStyle + policy UI); the mount keeps passing `offlineOnly` until the
owner opts in — opt-in is a native control of the instrument, never a
silent fetch. Acceptance: offline default identical to today; opting in
shows imagery AND the attribution; opting out returns to the offline
ground; refusal/reasons surface verbatim when a provider is absent.
